title: Real-Time Multi-Tenant CRM Analytics & Aggregation Engine
businessContext: A B2B SaaS platform provides live customer pipeline analytics to 10,000 corporate tenants (from small startups with 1,000 events to Fortune 500 enterprises with 50,000,000 events). Running analytical queries (e.g. "Conversion rate by lead source over last 90 days") directly on the operational PostgreSQL OLTP database is freezing transactional tables and causing multi-tenant noisy-neighbor outages.
problemStatement: Architect a segregated OLAP analytics pipeline that ingests real-time events, isolates tenant data, powers interactive sub-second dashboard queries, and guarantees that a massive enterprise tenant running complex queries does not degrade performance for other tenants.
constraints: Sub-second query response time (P95 < 500ms) for arbitrary time-range aggregations.
Data freshness / lag: events visible in analytics dashboard within 10 seconds of occurrence.
Tenant noisy-neighbor isolation: strict resource limits per tenant tier.

systemDesignReqs.scale: 10,000 tenants, 100M events ingested / day, 200 concurrent analytical dashboard queries / sec.
functional: Real-time ingestion of CRM events (leads created, emails sent, deals won).
Interactive filtering by date range, sales rep, territory, and deal stage.
Role-Based multi-tenant data isolation (tenant A cannot view tenant B data).
nonFunctional: Zero impact on OLTP database performance.
Cost-effective storage tiering (hot 90 days vs cold historical).
assumptions: OLTP uses PostgreSQL for relational transactional integrity.
OLAP needs columnar storage (ClickHouse / StarRocks / Snowflake / BigQuery).

candidateTasks: Design the Lambda / Kappa architecture data flow from PostgreSQL OLTP -> Kafka -> Stream Processor / Columnar OLAP (ClickHouse) -> Analytics API.
Design the ClickHouse table schema with sorting key `(tenant_id, event_date, event_type)` for tenant isolation and index pruning.
Explain how columnar storage compression and vectorized execution achieve 100x speedup over row-oriented databases.
Implement tenant rate limiting and query concurrency quotas at the Analytics Gateway.
hints: Row-oriented databases (Postgres) read entire 50-column rows from disk even if you only aggregate 1 column.
Columnar databases (ClickHouse) only read the specific columns requested, compressed with ZSTD/LZ4, scanning millions of rows per millisecond.
alternativeApproaches: PostgreSQL with TimescaleDB / Citus extension for smaller scale (< 50M events).
commonMistakes: Creating separate database tables or schemas for each of the 10,000 tenants in ClickHouse (leads to metadata explosion and file descriptor exhaustion).
Ingesting events row-by-row into ClickHouse: ClickHouse requires micro-batches (e.g. 5,000+ rows per insert) to prevent part-creation thrashing.
